meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тоять'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'stop', paired with 'постоять'.

examples.text: Я постоянно с людьми работаю.
examples.trans: I work with people all the time.

examples.text: Вы просто настоящие уроды оба!
examples.trans: The two of you are simply total idiots!

examples.text: Ты сам настоящий псих, понял меня?
examples.trans: You are a real psycho yourself, got that?

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'wait', paired with 'ждать'.

examples.text: Подожди, я сейчас.
examples.trans: Wait, I'll be right there.

examples.text: Подождите минуту.
examples.trans: Wait a minute.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'говорить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'finished speaking'.

examples.text: Хорошо, договорились, приходи на час позже.
examples.trans: Alright, it is a deal, come an hour later.

examples.text: Да, вот мы и договорились.
examples.trans: Yes, then it is settled between us.

examples.text: Хорошо, Макс, мы с тобой договорились.
examples.trans: Alright, Max, we have a deal.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Может, ещё не всё потеряно?
examples.trans: Maybe not everything is lost yet?

examples.text: Может, пойдём вечером кофе попьём?
examples.trans: Maybe we could go have some coffee tonight?

examples.text: Шеф, можно к вам на секунду?
examples.trans: Chef, may I speak with you for a second?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'to, towards', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Плотный завтрак и чашечка горячего кофе.
examples.trans: A hearty breakfast and a little cup of hot coffee.

examples.text: Ты опять за Катей подглядывал?
examples.trans: Were you peeking at Katya again?

examples.text: Наш Лёва запал на дочку шефа.
examples.trans: Our Lyova has fallen for the Chef's daughter.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Для тебя это дело привычное.
examples.trans: For you this kind of thing is familiar.

examples.text: С красивыми, умными, интеллигентными людьми.
examples.trans: With handsome, smart, cultured people.

examples.text: Скажи мне, почему так вышло?
examples.trans: Tell me, why did it turn out like this?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'екунда'). Common feminine noun meaning 'second' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Шеф, можно к вам на секунду?
examples.trans: Chef, may I speak with you for a second?

examples.text: Подожди одну секунду, вот, возьми.
examples.trans: Wait one second, here, take this.

examples.text: Секунду. Сейчас я позвоню.
examples.trans: One second. I'll call right now.
